title: Rahul Yadav’s four-for leads Janakpur to NPL win

 Match Report Rahul Yadav takes four as Janakpur Bolts beat Kathmandu Gorkhas
 Moeen Ali and Saif Hassan shared an unbeaten 79-run stand as Janakpur chased 116 with 16 balls remaining.
 Nischal Tiwari + Follow 29 October 2026 · 21:04 NPT 
 Save Share A A A Rahul Yadav celebrates a wicket for Janakpur Bolts during the Nepal Premier League 2026 at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur. Listen to this article 3 min KATHMANDU, October 29: Rahul Yadav took four wickets before Moeen Ali and Saif Hassan completed a controlled chase as Janakpur Bolts defeated Kathmandu Gorkhas by eight wickets in Match 5 of the Nepal Premier League 2026 at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur on Thursday.
 Score summary: Kathmandu Gorkhas 115 in 19.3 overs (Bhim Sharki 33; Rahul Yadav 4 for 31, Saif Hassan 2 for 11) lost to Janakpur Bolts 116/2 in 17.2 overs (Moeen Ali 58 not out, Saif Hassan 40 not out) by eight wickets.
 Kathmandu won the toss and chose to bat, but Rahul struck with his first delivery for the second match in succession. Sam Heazlett made one before he was caught by Moeen, and Harishankar Sah fell to Saif in the final over of the powerplay.
 Rahul then removed Smit Patel for 13, leaving Kathmandu 29/3 in the sixth over. Rashid Khan made 17 off 14 balls before Moeen dismissed him, while Bhim tried to hold the innings together with 33 off 29 balls, including four fours.

 The decisive sequence came after Kathmandu had reached 92/5. Lalit Rajbanshi removed Bhim before Rahul dismissed Karan KC and Aadil Alam with successive deliveries in the 17th over. Rahul then caught Jahandad Khan from Saif's next ball as Kathmandu slipped to 99/9, losing four wickets for seven runs.
 Ripon Mondol and Shahab Alam added 16 for the final wicket before Harmeet Singh dismissed Ripon for nine. Kathmandu were bowled out for 115 with three deliveries unused.
 Rahul finished with 4 for 31 from four overs, following his 2 for 15 against Karnali Yaks on his NPL debut. The 16-year-old has now taken six wickets in his first two appearances. Saif returned 2 for 11 from four overs, while Moeen, Harmeet and Lalit took one wicket each.
 Janakpur lost Trit Raj Das for five in the second over of their chase. Mayan Yadav made nine before being run out in the sixth over, leaving the Bolts 37/2.
 Moeen and Saif denied Kathmandu another opening. They added an unbeaten 79 for the third wicket, taking Janakpur to the target in 17.2 overs. Moeen finished on 58 off 51 balls, with three fours and three sixes, while Saif made an unbeaten 40 off 39 balls, striking one four and three sixes.
 The partnership reached 50 from 54 balls before the pair accelerated. Moeen completed his half-century from 49 deliveries, and Saif finished the match with a six as Janakpur secured their first victory of the season following their 19-run defeat to Karnali Yaks.
 Janakpur captain Harmeet described Rahul as “one of the finds of this tournament” after the match.
 “I hope he keeps his head on his shoulders and continues performing,” Harmeet said. “That's what this league is all about: discovering talented cricketers like him.”
 Rahul, who was named Player of the Match, said the opportunity to share the dressing room with experienced players was helping his development.
 “I'm learning a lot because I'm the youngest player in our team,” he said. “I'm getting as many opportunities as possible to learn from the senior players.”
 Janakpur will next face Pokhara Avengers in Kirtipur on November 1.
